mathWordsOfTheDay.definition: A drafting constraint that places points at permitted increments or locations.
The permitted variation from a target measurement.
A named organizational level used to control visibility, locking, editing, and communication of related drawing objects.
The proportional relationship between a representation and the corresponding real object or space.
A measurable amount expressed with a number and an appropriate unit.
A rule that maps every point of a figure to an image point.
A mathematically defined geometric representation or directed quantity; in digital graphics, vector shapes are stored through points, lines, and curves rather than a fixed pixel grid.

terms.definition: Computer-aided design or drafting used to construct, measure, organize, and communicate precise geometric models.
A visible reference framework of regularly spaced lines or points used to orient a drawing.
A drafting constraint that places points at permitted increments or locations.
The declared extent or sheet/site region in which a drawing is organized.
A numerical annotation communicating a measured or specified geometric size.
The permitted variation from a target measurement.
The absolute difference between a measured value and an accepted or target value.
Absolute error compared with the size of the accepted or target value, often expressed as a percent.
Digits used to communicate measurement precision without implying unsupported accuracy.
A named organizational level for controlling related drawing objects.
A collection of selected objects treated together for editing while remaining on one or more layers.
A state that prevents unintended editing of selected geometry or a layer.
The proportional relationship between drawing and actual dimensions.
The unobstructed usable width of a passage or opening.
The planned paths through and between spaces or objects.
A requirement or limit that a valid design must satisfy.
A measurable amount stated with a number and unit.
An organized record of required materials, calculated quantities, adjustments, units, and assumptions.
An allowance added to a base material quantity for cutting, breakage, pattern matching, defects, or other project conditions.
A rule mapping a preimage to an image.
A property that remains unchanged under a specified transformation.
A repeatable geometric component used to build a larger design system.
A symmetry in which a figure maps onto itself after a rotation smaller than 360 degrees.
Mathematically represented geometry that can scale without dependence on a fixed pixel grid.
The editable original file preserving the structure needed for continued development.
A file format intended to transfer geometric information between compatible tools or workflows.
Checking an output by measuring a known dimension or scale bar rather than trusting visual appearance or settings alone.
A concise argument that supports design decisions with geometric evidence, constraints, calculations, verification, and revision.
